body.statement: For every \(\mathbf P=(P_n)\in\mathcal B_{\epsilon,M,c_0,v_0,v_1}\), \(\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{HL}}-\tau(P_n)=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n\phi_{P_n}(O_i)+o_{Q_{P_n}^{(n)}}(n^{-1/2})\), \(\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{HL}}-\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{OS}}=o_{Q_{P_n}^{(n)}}(n^{-1/2})\), \(\widehat V^{\mathrm{HL}}/V_{\mathrm{eff}}(P_n)\to1\), and \(\widehat V^{\mathrm{OS}}/V_{\mathrm{eff}}(P_n)\to1\) in \(Q_{P_n}^{(n)}\)-probability. In addition, \(\widehat R^{\mathrm{HL}}-z_{1-\alpha/2}\sqrt{\widehat V^{\mathrm{HL}}/n}=o_{Q_{P_n}^{(n)}}(n^{-1/2})\) and \(\sqrt n\{\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{HL}}-\tau(P_n)\}/\sqrt{V_{\mathrm{eff}}(P_n)}\Rightarrow N(0,1)\).
body.justification: The same globally honest construction must recover the semiparametric first-order law when empty-cell bias is locally negligible.
body.gap: ZengBalakrishnanHanKennedy2024, Appendix A.1, records a saturated plug-in Gaussian regime while its categorical model permits arbitrary and zero cell masses; the balanced lower-mass condition here is a separately imposed local restriction used only for linearization. ChernozhukovEtAl2018DML, Theorem 5.1, assumes nuisance product rates, and neither paper controls the nonlinear rare-cell correction and robust critical radius of a globally honest procedure.
body.consumer: Efficient standard errors and familiar Gaussian reporting when the categorical table is sufficiently populated, without changing procedures across regimes.

obligation.what_is_open: The first-order equivalence, ratio-consistent variance, and Gaussian-radius expansion for the heavy-light outputs.
obligation.obstruction: The saturated one-step comparator is explicit and its nuisance rates follow from balanced cells, but the heavy-light estimator, variance output, and radius are not explicit maps. Nothing in the frozen handles states that the rare branch switches off, that the heavy branch equals the one-step score to first order, or that its direct critical value converges to the Gaussian quantile.
obligation.attempted: I derived the saturated-cell nuisance rates, orthogonal remainder, empirical-process remainder, variance consistency, and Lyapunov condition. The same comparison cannot be written for the unnamed heavy-light summands.
obligation.partial_result:
The saturated comparator part can be derived from the frozen assumptions.  If
\(g(O;\eta)\) denotes the augmented inverse-propensity score in
\(def:saturated\text{-}one\text{-}step\), then for every training fold,
binomial reciprocal-count identities and the conditional second-moment bound
implied by \(ass:conditional\text{-}fourth\text{-}moment\) give
\[
 \sum_kp_k(\widehat\mu_{ak}-\mu_{ak})^2=O_P(d_n/n),
 \qquad
 \sum_kp_k(\widehat\pi_k-\pi_k)^2=O_P(d_n/n).
\]
Conditional expectation of the score difference equals
\[
 \sum_kp_k(\widehat\pi_k-\pi_k)
 \left\{\frac{\widehat\mu_{1k}-\mu_{1k}}{\widehat\pi_k}
 +\frac{\widehat\mu_{0k}-\mu_{0k}}{1-\widehat\pi_k}\right\},
\]
whose absolute value is \(O_P(d_n/n)=o_P(n^{-1/2})\) by clipped overlap and
\(d_n=o(\sqrt n)\).  Conditional variance of the centered score difference is
\(O_P(d_n/n)\), so cross-fitting makes its empirical average
\(O_P(\sqrt{d_n}/n)=o_P(n^{-1/2})\).  Hence
\[
 \widehat\tau^{\mathrm{OS}}-\tau(P_n)
 =n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n\phi_{P_n}(O_i)+o_P(n^{-1/2}).
\]
The envelope and overlap assumptions give
\(E_{P_n}|\phi_{P_n}|^4\le C_\epsilon M^4\); therefore the oracle empirical
second moment converges to \(V_{\mathrm{eff}}(P_n)\), and the preceding
score-difference bound gives
\(\widehat V^{\mathrm{OS}}/V_{\mathrm{eff}}(P_n)\to1\).  The same fourth-moment
bound verifies the Lyapunov ratio, so the standardized oracle sum, and hence
the one-step estimator, is asymptotically standard normal.  What is not derived
is any corresponding assertion about the undefined heavy-light outputs.
